website_request:
Redesign the public website for Paul's Trailer Service Inc. as an original, polished one-page site. First assess the source website in this same Duck.ai conversation, then use that assessment as the factual source for the redesign. Present the business history, trailer repair services, trailer types served, parts support, and clear contact options. Make calling the shop the primary conversion action and include a strong, image-led hero. Write original copy and do not invent facts. The workflow will request CSS first in three labeled parts, then send "acknowledged," then request HTML in three labeled parts in the same chat. Keep the files compatible as index.html and styles.css.
Treat the source site as authoritative only for details Duck.ai can cite from pages on that domain; leave other details unknown.
In the audit, clearly separate observed facts from inferred audience and design opinions.
design_brief: Audience: trailer owners and fleet operators who need dependable service or parts support. Visual direction: established industrial service company with a modern editorial feel; deep navy, warm off-white, and restrained safety-orange accents; bold condensed display type with highly readable body text; documentary trailer-shop imagery and subtle technical drawing details. Use varied section layouts, strong hierarchy, one primary call-to-call CTA, and a mobile layout designed deliberately rather than merely stacked. After the source assessment, adapt one fitting named HTML5 UP template as structural inspiration. Keep the template name, source URL, CC BY 3.0 license URL, and adaptation note in a non-rendering HTML comment; do not show a template credit. Do not copy the source website's text, logo, or photographs. Use original wording and appropriately licensed relevant images.
